newsitem.title: GERMANY: Allianz says merger ups home competition. [CORRECTED 13:50 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Allianz says merger ups home competition. [CORRECTED 13:50 GMT]

text.p: German insurance market leader Allianz AG on Friday said it expected tougher times ahead in its domestic market after news of a merger that will create a significant rival.

Muenchener Rueckversicherung AG (Munich Re), announced overnight it would acquire Victoria Holding AG by merging it with its Hamburg-Mannheimer AG unit to create the second largest insurance group in Germany.
"We are expecting tougher competition on the German market," said Allianz spokesman Emilio Galli-Zugaro, who agreed the move presented a challenge.
"This is certainly a positive development for customers and for the market," he added, noting that the new group, to be called ERGO, would be a welcome addition to the stock market.
Allianz confirmed that it still held a 20 percent stake in the Hamburg Mannheimer Holding group and 20 percent (corrects from ten percent) of Hamburg-Mannheimer Sach, the company's non-life unit.
Galli-Zugaro said the company had no immediate plans to part from those holdings, but that a change could come in the future since the merger would dilute the stakes and make them "fungible".
He also noted that the merger was a logical move in light of the liberalisation of the European insurance market which has already led to mega-mergers such as the fusion of UAP and AXA in France.
